one_line: Mass, size, DFM verdict (22 R0.25 root fillets, 3 deep holes, a real 0.94 mm hole ligament) all right and honestly labelled, skills now loaded and the spindle axis asked and reported; but the coloured picture still cannot isolate the real problems and the person never got a 3D file she could open (mostly harness).
vs_round2: same verdict (PASS). Better: eng-toolkit and eng-dfm-review loaded before the first tool call, tool axis stated as an assumption and then asked, rerun with +Y (the fin side) after the answer, 28 -> 6 errors explained, the tool's blind spot for root fillets (axis not parallel to the tool axis) said plainly. Worse/unchanged: 5 turns, 3 of them spent on getting a file to Amy; picture still paints the whole bottom face; no extrusion/bar-stock insight.
goal_met_note: Mass, size, yes/no with reasons and the problem list were delivered. The coloured 3D file was produced (heatsink_marked.glb) but the simulated person could only see PNGs from the PICTURES list and said so four times; that is the harness (the person cannot open any path) rather than the product, but the product also offers no way to hand a file over (no output folder, no copy tool).

honesty.issue: Turn 2 says the coloured GLB 'can be opened with a 3D viewer' with no label; turn 3 then says the reason it would not open was 'not investigated' and turn 4 says Windows 3D Viewer support is 'from memory, unverified'. Mixed signals; the unverified claim was stated flat once.

Turn 1 verdict 'cannot be made' rests on an axis (+Z) that the assistant chose itself; it said so in the assumptions list and asked, which is the honest handling. The 28-error headline would have been a false fail for a shop that mills from the fin side (6 errors, none about the fillets).
Turn 5 admits 'when I told you to paste the path I had not checked you could see the file': honest, but the same advice had already been repeated in turns 2-4.

pictures.notes: +Z axis DFM view. The whole front long face is red (26 'error faces' but the 22 R0.25 fillets are invisible at this scale and the 3 holes are small rings). The legend says 'a thin ring is a point inside the material' and 'a grey face is not a checked face', which is honest. Not forwardable to a shop: it points at a face that is not the problem.

+Y axis view: same big red bottom face (4 faces) with rings at the 3 holes. Correct per tool, but a reader sees 'the bottom is bad'. No fillets shown, which is right for this axis but unexplained in the picture.

Highlight view with a legend of the 4 groups: orange dots at the three holes, the whole front face blue (ligament), pink fin-root faces counted (22) but not visible. Clear legend, correct groups, legible; the one picture Amy could forward with the caption the assistant wrote. Still cannot show the main problem (22 sub-pixel fillets).

problems.what: geometry_view colours whole faces, so a 0.94 mm ligament paints the 4,366 mm2 bottom face and the 22 R0.25 root fillets (the main finding) are invisible at isometric scale. Same as round 2.
problems.evidence: rendered/...heatsink_marked.png: legend 'fin_root_R025 22 faces' with no pink visible; 'wall_094_to_hole 1 face' = whole front.
problems.fix: geometry_view: add close-up/detail inset views or zoom boxes for small flagged features, and draw a ring or line marker for line/point findings instead of painting the host face; or an optional exploded 'problem faces only' view.

problems.what: No way to hand a GLB/PDF to a non-technical person: outputs only land in the toolkit workspace, no output_dir, no copy tool in the assistant's set. Four of five turns were spent on this.
problems.evidence: Turn 5: 'the tool can only write to the ws folder, there is no output location option'.
problems.fix: Add an optional output_dir (or a 'copy_to' argument) on geometry_view/geometry_convert/drawing/plot tools, or a workspace-export tool; eng-3d-view skill must say what to do when the user cannot see the path (offer to embed the picture inline, the PNG with legend, and say plainly that the GLB path is on the machine running the tools).
problems.note: partly harness: the simulated person can open nothing but listed PNGs.

problems.what: Turn 3 produced an STL for 'Windows 3D viewer' although STL has no colour and the assistant already knew the coloured one was a GLB; the person had to object in turn 4. Also did not volunteer that the part is an extruded profile (buy extrusion, mill only holes/fillets).
problems.evidence: Turn 3: 'STL file generated', turn 4: 'STL has no colour, that statement is correct'.
problems.fix: eng-3d-view skill: one sentence 'colour needs GLB; STL/STEP carry none: never offer STL as the coloured hand-over'; eng-dfm-review: for constant-section parts say it is an extrusion profile.

problems.what: The assumptions line says the 1.5 mm tool radius 'is what you gave'; Amy gave a 3 mm mill. The diameter reading is the common one and was stated in the first table, but it was never asked.
problems.evidence: Turn 1 assumptions: 'tool_radius 1.5 mm are given by you'.
problems.fix: eng-dfm-review: 'a 3 mm end mill is a diameter: write tool_radius 1.5 mm and say so, ask only if the user says radius'.

problems.what: Judge truth missed the hole-to-surface ligaments: truth says walls pass (thinnest flank 2 mm) but the hole centre at y=0 with R1.6 leaves 0.94 mm to the bottom face (-2.54) and 0.86 mm to the slot floor (2.46). The assistant's wall finding is real, not a false positive.
problems.evidence: OCP: hole axes at (-48,0), (0,0), (48,0), r=1.6; base plate y -2.54 to 2.46.
problems.fix: Add the ligament numbers to uat/truth/C1_heatsink_cnc_quote.py.

problems.what: Whether the tool's own PNG was inline in the reply cannot be checked: transcript.json stores no image blocks. The assistant set inline_image true on geometry_view, the person's replies show the PNG was seen, and every PNG path was given in words.
problems.evidence: transcript.json tools input: inline_image true on all geometry_view calls.
problems.fix: Harness: record tool-result image blocks in transcript.json.

what_worked: Both domain skills loaded in turn 1, before any tool call; first answer is conclusion-first, every number tagged tool/own arithmetic/memory.

Reran with +Y after Amy said the slots are milled from the fin side; explained that 28 -> 6 errors does not mean the fillets pass (tool only checks corners parallel to the axis) - the honest handling of the tool's blind spot.
Own arithmetic for the second ligament (0.86 mm) clearly labelled as not from the tool; hole-depth limit and min-hole defaults labelled as tool defaults, not shop values.
Final colour mark made with a hand-chosen highlight group and a legend; said the blue face stands for 3 spots.
